summary: Built a small Python LangChain-based sample that demonstrates encoding transactions as embeddings, storing synthetic fraud-pattern vectors in an Azure DocumentDB collection, and scoring new transactions by searching for similar patterns. The sample attempts a best-effort server-side vector index creation but falls back to client-side cosine similarity when server-side vector features or exact syntax are unavailable. The repository includes a seed script, FastAPI app, a one-shot demo, and unit tests. I verified dependency installation, tests, seeding the live cluster (using DOCUMENTDB_URI), and ran the demo scoring run locally against the live cluster. Real OpenAI embeddings were not used because OPENAI_API_KEY was not set during verification; the sample falls back to deterministic mock embeddings so the demo runs without secrets.
how_to_run:
1) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
2) Copy .env.example to .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI (and optionally OPENAI_API_KEY)
3) python seed_data.py    # creates collection and inserts synthetic pattern docs (best-effort server-side index creation)
4) Start the API (optional): uvicorn src.app:app --reload
   Or run the one-shot demo which exercises the agent without starting a server: python run_demo.py
5) To run tests: pytest

Notes:
- Do not put secrets in the repository. DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (optional) are read from environment variables.
- The sample uses the existing database sample_fintech_01 as required.
- If you set OPENAI_API_KEY, the agent will attempt to use LangChain OpenAIEmbeddings; otherwise deterministic mock embeddings are used so the sample remains runnable.
verification_done: python seed_data.py: created collection 'fraud_patterns', attempted simple server-side embedding index creation (best-effort), inserted 12 pattern documents, wrote sample_transactions.json
python run_demo.py: scored 5 sample transactions and printed risk_score, explanation and matches using client-side similarity (demo output printed)
not_verified: Exact server-side vector-index creation syntax and parameters for the target DocumentDB cluster (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN, vectorOptions keys, createIndex parameter names). The seed script performed a best-effort create_index and continued on error; the precise API surface for vector index creation was not verified against official docs in this run. (Reason: readiness report highlighted information gaps and no MCP/learn server was available to programmatically verify exact syntax.)

Server-side vector search operator/aggregation syntax (e.g., $search with vector semantics, knn-style operators and their names). The agent implements a best-effort placeholder for server-side search but falls back to client-side cosine similarity if server-side operators are unavailable or reject queries.

End-to-end behavior using real embeddings from OpenAI via LangChain. OPENAI_API_KEY was not set in the environment during verification, so the agent used deterministic mock embeddings. To verify production-grade embedding behavior, set OPENAI_API_KEY and re-run seed_data.py (to generate embeddings with the real model) and run the demo or API.

Any advanced performance characteristics (index tuning like nlists/probes, IVF/HNSW parameters) on the live cluster were not tuned or measured in this sample; those require access to official index options and performance testing beyond a small sample.
open_issues: If you want server-side vector indexing and search, consult the DocumentDB (managed MongoDB-compatible) official docs for the exact createIndex vectorOptions and aggregation/operator names (e.g., specific $search/$vectorSearch stage names). Update seed_data.py to use the verified syntax and parameters. (The readiness report recommended verifying these before committing; I left a fallback in place.)
When enabling real embeddings (OPENAI_API_KEY), you may need to re-seed patterns so their stored embeddings are produced by the chosen model and dimension; update EMBED_DIM assumptions if necessary.

The demo uses client-side similarity for correctness and portability; for production workloads, you should create and tune a proper server-side vector index supported by the DocumentDB cluster for scalability and latency.
